nodes.label: aspire-deployment skill
nodes.author: Microsoft
nodes.rationale: Deployment starts from the AppHost model; Aspire-native deploy wins over generic cloud tools because Aspire handles publish/deploy/destroy end-to-end.

nodes.label: aspire-monitoring skill
nodes.author: Microsoft
nodes.rationale: The CLI talks to a running AppHost over a local backchannel socket by design, so deployed apps route to platform tools.

nodes.label: aspire-orchestration skill
nodes.author: Microsoft
nodes.rationale: Guardrails prevent agent self-harm (file locks, orphaned processes) documented in microsoft/aspire#15801.

nodes.label: Aspireify Skill
nodes.author: Microsoft
nodes.rationale: One-time wiring skill that turns an aspire init skeleton into a working AppHost, then self-deactivates and hands off to aspire-orchestration

nodes.label: Seed Test Concept
nodes.rationale: Seed lands the page in the state every scenario starts from; always go through the test rather than opening the URL to capture custom setup

nodes.label: Deploy to Azure Container Apps
nodes.rationale: PostgreSQL, Redis and RabbitMQ deploy as containers — intended for evaluation/demos, not production data.

nodes.label: CI/CD and GitHub Actions deployment reference
nodes.norm_label: ci/cd and github actions deployment reference

nodes.label: Docker Compose deployment reference
nodes.rationale: Bind mount sources are placeholderized because local paths often do not exist on another Docker host.

nodes.label: JavaScript app deployment reference
nodes.rationale: A Vite dev server is build-only during publish unless the AppHost selects who serves the built files.

nodes.label: Kubernetes and AKS deployment reference
nodes.rationale: A container registry is required for vanilla Kubernetes because Aspire has no local-registry fallback.

nodes.label: Common deployment preflight reference
nodes.rationale: Don't pipe prompting commands through tee/tail since pipes remove the interactive terminal selection prompts need.

nodes.label: Tiered Resource Modeling Preference (First-party > Community Toolkit > Raw)
nodes.community_name: AppHost Wiring and API Lookup Reference
nodes.norm_label: tiered resource modeling preference (first-party > community toolkit > raw)
nodes.rationale: Typed integrations handle working dirs, port injection, health checks and dashboard integration; raw AddExecutable/AddContainer are last resort

nodes.label: Prefer HTTPS and Aspire-Managed Ports
nodes.community_name: AppHost Wiring and API Lookup Reference
nodes.rationale: Managed ports avoid collisions and allow multiple AppHosts side-by-side; pin fixed ports only for OAuth callbacks, hardcoded clients, or tooling

nodes.label: Persistent Container Lifetime and Stale Volume Auth Failures
nodes.community_name: AppHost Wiring and API Lookup Reference
nodes.norm_label: persistent container lifetime and stale volume auth failures
nodes.rationale: Persistent lifetime prevents data loss across restarts, but auto-generated passwords stored in volumes can mismatch after AppHost recreation

nodes.label: Avoid Secrets in WithArgs
nodes.community_name: AppHost Wiring and API Lookup Reference
nodes.rationale: Process arguments are visible in ps output, task managers and logs — secret leakage risk; pass secrets via environment variables

nodes.label: WaitFor / WaitForCompletion Dependency Ordering
nodes.community_name: AppHost Wiring and API Lookup Reference

nodes.label: WithReference vs WithEnvironment
nodes.community_name: AppHost Wiring and API Lookup Reference
nodes.rationale: WithReference injects connection info and enables service discovery; WithEnvironment for custom config. Never hand-build connection strings when WithReference works

nodes.label: Do Not Model Passwords for Typed Integrations
nodes.community_name: AppHost Wiring and API Lookup Reference
nodes.norm_label: do not model passwords for typed integrations
nodes.rationale: Typed integrations auto-generate secure passwords; Compose needed them only because it doesn't manage credentials

nodes.label: Skip withYarn in Workspace Monorepos
nodes.community_name: AppHost Wiring and API Lookup Reference
nodes.rationale: Concurrent per-resource yarn installs on shared node_modules cause EPERM file-lock errors on Windows and are redundant

nodes.label: eShop.AppHost (Aspire AppHost)
nodes.rationale: Root aspire.config.json selects src/eShop.AppHost/eShop.AppHost.csproj to avoid ambiguity with test AppHosts.

nodes.label: Safety guardrails reference
nodes.rationale: dotnet run bypasses orchestration (no dashboard/backchannel); dotnet build while Aspire runs hits MSB3491/CS2012 locks; curl polling ignores dynamic ports and dependency ordering.

nodes.label: Large Solution Triage and Core Loop Wiring
nodes.norm_label: large solution triage and core loop wiring
nodes.rationale: Core loop is a risk-reduction strategy: validate the minimal set first, then add services 2-3 at a time

nodes.label: Legacy IHostBuilder vs IHostApplicationBuilder Detection
nodes.rationale: ServiceDefaults targets IHostApplicationBuilder; do not create adapter extensions on IHostBuilder — either skip ServiceDefaults or modernize bootstrap

nodes.label: Nested global.json for Mixed SDK Repos
nodes.norm_label: nested global.json for mixed sdk repos
nodes.rationale: AppHost must stay on current Aspire-supported SDK while root global.json and existing TFMs remain unchanged

nodes.label: aspire wait over curl loops (displayName gotcha)
nodes.norm_label: aspire wait over curl loops (displayname gotcha)
nodes.rationale: aspire wait uses the AppHost's own health model; hand-rolled curl loops race with startup and can't see container-internal health

nodes.label: --non-interactive Flag Requirement
nodes.rationale: Without it the command can hang waiting for input

nodes.label: Never Edit .aspire/modules Rule
nodes.rationale: .aspire/modules is generated from apphost.ts and integration packages; edits are clobbered on next build, aspire add, or aspire start

nodes.label: Minimize Changes to User Code Principle
nodes.norm_label: minimize changes to user code principle
nodes.rationale: Adapt the AppHost to fit the app; prefer WithEnvironment matching existing env names and do not restructure directories unless the user chooses that tradeoff

nodes.label: Redis TLS Edge Case (WithoutHttpsCertificate)
nodes.rationale: Aspire auto-provisions TLS certs for containers; if Redis health checks fail with TLS errors use WithoutHttpsCertificate rather than falling back to AddContainer

nodes.label: Unified withEnvironment API
nodes.rationale: Single API handles all value kinds; per-kind helpers (withEnvironmentEndpoint, withEnvironmentParameter, etc.) are deprecated
